evals.query: In a React 19.3 app (no framework, client only), build a 'Rename' form: an input, a submit button that shows 'Saving...' while pending, an error message from the server, and the new name shown immediately before the server answers. The API is `async function updateName(name): Promise<{ error?: string }>`. Use the built-in React APIs for this, not a form library.
expected_behavior: Uses useActionState with an action whose signature is (prevState, formData) and reads the name with formData.get
Passes the dispatch function to <form action={...}> rather than handling onSubmit with preventDefault
Shows the pending state either from the isPending value of useActionState or from useFormStatus called in a child component of the form, never in the component that renders the form
Uses useOptimistic to show the new name before the server answers, calling the optimistic setter inside the action or a Transition
Notes that state updates placed after an await in a Transition must be wrapped in another startTransition, or avoids that case by returning the state from the action
Does not use the removed ReactDOM.useFormState
Replaces the isClient state and Effect with use(browser()), importing browser from react-dom
Wraps the component in a <Suspense> boundary with a fallback so the server renders the fallback
Does not recommend typeof window checks in render, a mounted flag, or throwing on the server to skip server rendering
Explains why the old pattern is discouraged (extra render or mismatch) without inventing APIs beyond the docs
Rewrites FancyInput as a plain function that receives ref as a prop, without forwardRef
Replaces defaultProps with an ES default parameter, such as label = 'Name'
Removes propTypes, noting React 19 ignores them and suggesting TypeScript
Renders <ThemeContext value="dark"> instead of <ThemeContext.Provider>
Passes an argument to useRef, such as useRef(null), as React 19 types require
Imports act from react instead of react-dom/test-utils and awaits it with an async callback
Removes eslint-plugin-react-compiler and uses the recommended preset of eslint-plugin-react-hooks, which carries the compiler rules
